subcategories.name: Traditional Braces
subcategories.text: Fixed brackets and wires that move teeth gradually into position. Suitable for most alignment and bite problems.

subcategories.name: Kids' Braces
subcategories.text: Early orthodontic care that guides the way a child's teeth and jaws grow, so problems are easier to correct.

subcategories.name: Myofunctional Appliances
subcategories.text: Removable appliances that help correct habits such as thumb sucking, tongue posture and mouth breathing, supporting healthy jaw development.

subcategories.name: Invisible Aligners
subcategories.text: Clear, removable trays that straighten teeth discreetly. Often used for mild to moderate alignment problems.

benefits: Straighter teeth and a smile you feel confident about
A better bite and more comfortable chewing
Teeth that are easier to clean, which supports gum health
Early correction of jaw and growth problems in children
Better balance between your teeth, jaws and lips

faq.q: How long does orthodontic treatment take?
faq.a: Most treatments take between about 12 and 24 months, depending on the problem and the appliance used. Your orthodontist will give you an estimate after examining you.

faq.q: Are invisible aligners as effective as traditional braces?
faq.a: Aligners work well for many mild to moderate cases. More complex problems may need braces. Your orthodontist will explain which option suits you.

faq.q: What is the ideal age for a child to see an orthodontist?
faq.a: A first check around the age of 7 is commonly recommended, so that any problems can be spotted early. Treatment may start then or later, depending on the child.

faq.q: Do braces hurt?
faq.a: Teeth can feel sore for a few days after braces are fitted or adjusted. This usually settles quickly and can be eased with simple pain relief if your orthodontist agrees.

faq.q: Can adults have braces?
faq.a: Yes. Orthodontic treatment is possible at any age as long as your teeth and gums are healthy.

subcategories.name: Crowns and Bridges
subcategories.text: Crowns cover and protect a damaged tooth. Bridges replace missing teeth. Both can be made from zirconia or ceramic for strength and a natural look.

subcategories.name: Jacket Crowns
subcategories.text: Tooth-coloured crowns that cover the whole tooth to restore its shape, size and appearance.

subcategories.name: Full Dentures
subcategories.text: A removable set of replacement teeth for a whole upper or lower arch.

subcategories.name: Partial Dentures
subcategories.text: A removable replacement for some missing teeth, held in place by the teeth you still have.

benefits: Restores your ability to chew and speak comfortably
Natural-looking teeth that match your smile
Protects weak or heavily filled teeth from breaking
Replaces missing teeth so neighbouring teeth do not drift
Long-lasting results with good care and regular check-ups

faq.q: What is the difference between a crown and a bridge?
faq.a: A crown covers a single damaged tooth. A bridge replaces one or more missing teeth by joining a false tooth to crowns on the teeth either side.

faq.q: Should I choose zirconia or ceramic?
faq.a: Both give a natural look. Zirconia is very strong, while ceramic can be very life-like. Your dentist will recommend the better material for the tooth and your bite.

faq.q: How long do crowns last?
faq.a: With good brushing, flossing and regular check-ups, crowns often last many years. The exact lifespan depends on the material, your bite and your oral hygiene.

faq.q: Is getting a crown painful?
faq.a: The tooth is numbed with local anaesthetic, so the treatment is comfortable. Mild sensitivity for a few days afterwards is normal.

faq.q: Are dentures uncomfortable?
faq.a: New dentures can feel strange at first. Most people adjust within a few weeks, and your dentist will adjust the fit if any area rubs.

subcategories.name: Single Tooth Implants
subcategories.text: A titanium post placed in the jawbone with a crown on top, to replace one missing tooth without involving the teeth next to it.

subcategories.name: Implant-Supported Bridges
subcategories.text: Several missing teeth replaced by a bridge that is anchored to implants rather than to natural teeth.

benefits: A fixed replacement that looks and feels like a natural tooth
Helps preserve the jawbone where a tooth is missing
Does not rely on the neighbouring teeth for support
Comfortable chewing and clear speech
A long-lasting solution with good care

faq.q: What is a dental implant?
faq.a: A dental implant is a small titanium post placed in the jawbone. Once it has bonded with the bone, a crown or bridge is fixed on top to replace the missing tooth or teeth.

faq.q: How long does implant treatment take?
faq.a: It usually takes several months, because the implant needs time to bond with the bone before the final crown is fitted. Your surgeon will give you a plan after your examination.

faq.q: Is the procedure painful?
faq.a: The area is numbed with local anaesthetic during surgery. Some swelling and soreness for a few days afterwards is normal and can be managed with the medicines your surgeon advises.

faq.q: Am I suitable for an implant?
faq.a: You need healthy gums and enough jawbone. An examination and X-rays will show whether implants are suitable for you or whether another option is better.

faq.q: How do I look after an implant?
faq.a: Brush and floss as you would for natural teeth and attend regular check-ups. Good hygiene is the best way to keep the implant healthy.

subcategories.name: Gingivectomy

subcategories.name: Disinfection

benefits: Relief from pain and infection
Treatment for problems that cannot be solved without surgery
Healthier gums and a better-fitting bite
Careful planning and aftercare from specialist surgeons
A clean, controlled setting for every procedure

faq.q: Is tooth extraction painful?
faq.a: The area is numbed before the tooth is removed, so you should feel pressure but not pain. Some soreness afterwards is normal and can be managed with the pain relief your dentist advises.

faq.q: What should I do after an extraction?
faq.a: Bite gently on the gauze, avoid rinsing hard or using a straw on the first day, keep the area clean as advised and call the clinic if bleeding or pain gets worse.

faq.q: What is an apicoectomy?
faq.a: It is a small operation to remove the tip of a tooth root and seal it when an infection does not clear after a root canal treatment. It can help save a tooth that would otherwise be lost.

faq.q: What is orthognathic surgery?
faq.a: It is surgery on the upper or lower jaw to correct the bite and the way the jaws fit together. It is planned carefully, often together with braces.

faq.q: How long is the recovery?
faq.a: It depends on the procedure. Simple extractions usually settle within days, while jaw surgery needs longer. Your surgeon will explain what to expect for your treatment.

subcategories.name: Root Canal Treatment
subcategories.text: The infected or damaged inside of the tooth is cleaned, disinfected and sealed so the tooth can stay in your mouth.

subcategories.name: Crown Restoration After Treatment
subcategories.text: A crown is often fitted over a treated tooth to protect it and restore its strength and appearance.

benefits: Relieves tooth pain and swelling caused by infection
Saves your natural tooth instead of removing it
Stops infection from spreading to the surrounding bone and gums
Lets you chew and smile normally again
Usually comfortable, as the tooth is numbed first

faq.q: Is a root canal treatment painful?
faq.a: The tooth is numbed with local anaesthetic, so the treatment should feel similar to having a filling. Mild soreness for a few days afterwards is common.

faq.q: How do I know if I need a root canal?
faq.a: Signs can include lasting sensitivity to hot or cold, pain when biting, swelling of the gum, or a tooth that has darkened. Only an examination and an X-ray can confirm it.

faq.q: How long does it take?
faq.a: Many teeth can be treated in one or two visits. Your dentist will tell you what to expect after examining the tooth.

faq.q: Will I need a crown afterwards?
faq.a: Often yes, especially for back teeth, because a treated tooth can be weaker. Your dentist will advise whether a crown is needed.

faq.q: What if I leave an infected tooth untreated?
faq.a: The infection can spread and cause more pain and swelling, and the tooth may eventually be lost. Early treatment gives the best chance of saving it.

faq.q: What is a Hollywood smile?
faq.a: It is a smile makeover that gives you bright, even, well-shaped teeth. Depending on your teeth it can include veneers, crowns and whitening.

faq.q: What is the difference between porcelain laminate, E.max and zirconia veneers?
faq.a: They are different materials. Porcelain laminate and E.max are very life-like, and zirconia is extremely strong. Your dentist will recommend the best one for your teeth and bite.

faq.q: Does teeth whitening damage the teeth?
faq.a: Professional whitening is considered safe when it is supervised by a dentist. Some people feel temporary sensitivity, which usually passes.

faq.q: How long do veneers last?
faq.a: With good oral hygiene and regular check-ups, veneers can last many years. Avoid biting hard objects and ask your dentist about a night guard if you grind your teeth.

faq.q: Is cosmetic treatment suitable for everyone?
faq.a: Your teeth and gums need to be healthy first. We will examine you and explain which options are suitable before any treatment starts.

benefits: Healthier gums and less bleeding
Fresher breath
Removal of plaque and tartar that causes decay and gum disease
Brighter teeth through stain removal
Early spotting of problems before they become painful

faq.q: How often should I have my teeth cleaned?
faq.a: Many people benefit from a professional clean about every six months. Your dentist will advise how often is right for you.

faq.q: Does scaling hurt?
faq.a: Most people feel only mild sensitivity. If your gums are sore, tell us and we will make the visit as comfortable as possible.

faq.q: Will cleaning make my teeth whiter?
faq.a: Cleaning removes surface stains, so teeth often look brighter. It does not change the natural colour of the tooth; whitening does that.

faq.q: Does scaling damage the enamel?
faq.a: No. When it is done properly, scaling removes deposits from the surface without harming the enamel.

faq.q: What does mouth hygiene guidance include?
faq.a: We show you how to brush and clean between your teeth properly and suggest products and habits that suit your mouth.

faq.q: What should I do if a tooth is knocked out?
faq.a: Pick the tooth up by the crown, not the root, and do not scrub it. Keep it moist, for example in milk, and come to the clinic as quickly as you can. Treatment is most successful when it is done within the first hour.

faq.q: What can I do about a severe toothache?
faq.a: Rinse gently with warm water, avoid very hot or cold food and call the clinic. Pain that lasts or comes with swelling or fever needs to be seen promptly.

faq.q: How do I know if my jaw may be broken?
faq.a: Signs include pain, swelling, a bite that feels different, numbness or difficulty opening the mouth after an injury. Seek care straight away.

faq.q: Should I call before I come?
faq.a: Yes, please call the clinic first so that we can prepare for you and tell you what to do on the way.

faq.q: What will happen at an emergency visit?
faq.a: We will relieve your pain, examine you, take any X-rays needed and explain the treatment. If more visits are needed we will arrange them.

faq.q: When should my child first see a dentist?
faq.a: A first visit is usually recommended when the first tooth appears or by the first birthday. Early visits help prevent problems.

faq.q: Do baby teeth really matter?
faq.a: Yes. Baby teeth help children chew and speak and hold space for the permanent teeth. Decay in baby teeth can cause pain and affect the teeth that follow.

faq.q: How do you help children feel comfortable?
faq.a: We explain what we are doing in simple words, take our time and make the visit as relaxed as possible.

faq.q: Does my child need a filling for a baby tooth?
faq.a: If the tooth has decay, treating it early prevents pain and infection. Your dentist will explain whether a filling is needed.

faq.q: How often should my child brush?
faq.a: Twice a day with a smear or small pea-sized amount of fluoride toothpaste, with a parent helping or checking until the child can brush well alone.

faq.q: How do I book an appointment?
faq.a: Use the appointment form on the Contact page, call the clinic, or message us on Telegram. We will confirm your time with you.

faq.q: What are your opening hours?
faq.a: We are open Monday to Saturday, 8:30 AM to 6:00 PM, and closed on Sundays.

faq.q: Where is the clinic?
faq.a: We are in the Abyssinia Building, 4th floor, Bole Medhanialem, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

faq.q: Do you treat children?
faq.a: Yes. Our pediatric service covers fillings, cleanings and baby tooth extraction, and kids braces are available.

faq.q: What should I do in a dental emergency?
faq.a: Call the clinic straight away. For a knocked-out tooth, keep the tooth moist and get to the clinic as quickly as you can.
